historical.merrill_analysis: -ameke attached to a verb functions as adjectivizer/nominalizer [participial], illustrated specifically with cotschimé-ameke < cotschimé ‘dormir’.
historical.steffel_general_ameke_analysis: source-explicit participial ending (Mittelwort); final ke reported as frequently omitted in pronunciation

issues_requiring_analysis: historical final -me in the lexical base versus modern base-final -i
comparison.prohibited_shortcut: Do not derive modern Cochí by mechanically stripping -me from historical Cotſchimé, and do not count old <tsch>~modern <ch> as a general sound law without independent correspondences.

strengths: Historical and modern bases share the core meaning ‘sleep/dormir’.
Historical X~X+ameke relation is explicitly participial in Merrill's analysis of Steffel and is directly attested in the historical lexicon.
Modern SRC-02 directly states Cochí ‘Dormir’ -> pp. cochíami.
The comparison therefore aligns lexical meaning and derivational function without depending on an automatically inferred modern exact-string pair.
next_steps: Search independent Rarámuri varieties for reflexes of the sleep root and participial forms.
Assemble independent historical-modern correspondences for <tsch>~<ch> and base-final -me~Ø/i before adjudicating formal continuity.
Keep the modern cochíami evidence as source-note-attested even if no independent headword exists in SRC-02.
